description: Recall and precision evals for the security-review skill. Positives (01-09) plant a known CWE; traps (10-12) are safe-but-tempting code that must not be flagged. Fixtures contain no answer-leaking comments; ground truth lives in GROUND_TRUTH.md.

evals.name: SQL injection (string concatenation)
evals.prompt: Do a deep security review of the code in evals/files/01-sqli/. List each finding with its class, file, severity, and confidence tier.
evals.expected_output: Reports a Confirmed SQL injection where the id parameter is concatenated into the query.
expectations: Reports a SQL injection (SQLi) finding in app.py
The SQL injection is rated Confirmed and High or Critical severity
The finding identifies the query built by string-concatenating request.args id
The output includes a coverage ledger and tiered findings

evals.name: OS command injection (shell=True)
evals.prompt: Do a deep security review of the code in evals/files/02-command-injection/. List each finding with class, file, severity, and confidence.
evals.expected_output: Reports a Confirmed OS command injection via shell=True with concatenated host input.
expectations: Reports an OS command injection finding in run.py
The finding references subprocess with shell=True and the concatenated host parameter
The command injection is rated Confirmed and High or Critical severity

evals.name: IDOR / broken object level authorization
evals.prompt: Do a deep security review of the code in evals/files/03-idor/. List each finding with class, file, severity, and confidence.
evals.expected_output: Reports broken access control / IDOR: any order id is returned with no ownership check.
expectations: Reports an IDOR or broken access control finding in app.py
The finding notes there is no ownership or authorization check tying the order to the current user
The finding is rated High severity

evals.name: Hardcoded credentials
evals.prompt: Do a deep security review of the code in evals/files/04-hardcoded-secret/. List each finding with class, file, severity, and confidence.
evals.expected_output: Reports hardcoded credentials (DB password and internal API token) in config.py.
expectations: Reports a hardcoded secret or credential finding in config.py
The finding identifies at least the DB_PASSWORD or INTERNAL_API_TOKEN as a hardcoded credential
The finding is rated Confirmed

evals.name: SSRF (server-side request forgery)
evals.prompt: Do a deep security review of the code in evals/files/05-ssrf/. List each finding with class, file, severity, and confidence.
evals.expected_output: Reports SSRF: the server fetches a user-supplied URL with no allowlist.
expectations: Reports an SSRF finding in fetch.py
The finding notes the fetched URL comes from user input with no allowlist or validation
The finding is rated Confirmed and High severity

evals.name: DOM-based XSS
evals.prompt: Do a deep security review of the code in evals/files/06-xss/. List each finding with class, file, severity, and confidence.
evals.expected_output: Reports XSS: user-controlled name is written to innerHTML.
expectations: Reports a cross-site scripting (XSS) finding in render.js
The finding identifies user-controlled input written to innerHTML
The finding is rated Confirmed

evals.name: Insecure deserialization
evals.prompt: Do a deep security review of the code in evals/files/07-deserialization/. List each finding with class, file, severity, and confidence.
evals.expected_output: Reports insecure deserialization: pickle.loads on untrusted request body.
expectations: Reports an insecure deserialization finding in loader.py
The finding references pickle.loads applied to untrusted request data
The finding is rated Confirmed and High or Critical severity

evals.name: Weak password hashing (MD5)
evals.prompt: Do a deep security review of the code in evals/files/08-weak-crypto/. List each finding with class, file, severity, and confidence.
evals.expected_output: Reports weak cryptography: MD5 used to hash passwords without a salt.
expectations: Reports a weak cryptography finding in auth.py
The finding identifies MD5 used for password hashing (fast, unsalted) as the problem
The finding recommends a password hashing function such as bcrypt, scrypt, or argon2

evals.name: Cross-file SQL injection (taint across files)
evals.prompt: Do a deep security review of the code in evals/files/09-crossfile-sqli/. List each finding with class, file, severity, and confidence.
evals.expected_output: Reports SQL injection traced from the acct parameter in routes.py into the sink in store.py.
expectations: Reports a SQL injection finding for the acct parameter

The finding names BOTH the source (request.args.get('acct') in routes.py) and the sink (con.execute in store.py) as one connected data path; a finding that only points at store.py without connecting it to the routes.py source does NOT pass
The SQL injection is rated Confirmed and High or Critical severity

evals.name: TRAP: parameterized query (safe)
evals.prompt: Do a deep security review of the code in evals/files/10-safe-parameterized/. List each finding with class, file, severity, and confidence.
evals.expected_output: No SQL injection: the query is parameterized. Any mention must not be a Confirmed SQLi.
expectations: Affirmatively states that db.py was reviewed (it does not skip or error on the file)
Does NOT report a Confirmed or High SQL injection vulnerability in db.py
Explicitly explains the query is safe because it uses a parameterized placeholder (?) with a params tuple

evals.name: TRAP: authorized object access (safe)
evals.prompt: Do a deep security review of the code in evals/files/11-safe-authz/. List each finding with class, file, severity, and confidence.
evals.expected_output: No IDOR: an ownership check gates the order. Any mention must not be a Confirmed IDOR.
expectations: Affirmatively states that app.py was reviewed (it does not skip or error on the file)
Does NOT report a Confirmed or High IDOR / broken access control vulnerability in app.py
Explicitly identifies the ownership check comparing the order's user_id to the session user as the control that makes it safe

evals.name: TRAP: bcrypt password hashing (safe)
evals.prompt: Do a deep security review of the code in evals/files/12-safe-bcrypt/. List each finding with class, file, severity, and confidence.
evals.expected_output: No weak-crypto finding: bcrypt with a per-hash salt is used correctly.
expectations: Affirmatively states that auth.py was reviewed (it does not skip or error on the file)
Does NOT report a Confirmed or High weak-cryptography vulnerability in auth.py
Explicitly identifies bcrypt with gensalt as an appropriate, salted password hashing choice
